name: Access Consciousness bars

card.summary: A light-touch head routine from the Access Consciousness movement, in which a practitioner rests fingers on 32 scalp points; participants use it for relaxation and a calmer self-image that they link to feeling and looking more at ease.
card.note: Sessions and facilitator courses carry costs; the wider organisation has drawn complaints and criticism from journalists and regulators.

quick.overview:
The Access Bars are a hands-on technique from the Access Consciousness movement. A practitioner lightly touches 32 points on the head while the client lies or sits quietly. Followers describe it as a way to release stored thoughts and feel calmer.

In looks terms, the claimed payoff is indirect: less tension and rumination, better sleep and a more relaxed face and posture. Proponents cite small studies; critics such as science communicator Jonathan Jarry have called that research poor, and note that relaxation from a scalp touch session may come from resting quietly.
quick.how: A facilitator touches the head points lightly for roughly an hour per session, often in a one-on-one booking or a group class. Some people take the entry course to practise on friends and family. People often pair it with other Access Consciousness classes or tools.
quick.risks: The technique itself is gentle touch. Reported concerns centre on cost (facilitator training was listed at AUD 30,000 in 2024), complaints lodged in Australia about marketing claims, and a Nova Scotia social worker who lost her licence in 2018 over inappropriate touching. People with health concerns are generally advised by clinicians to use standard medical care.

lead: The Access Consciousness bars (Access Bars) are a practice from the Access Consciousness movement, founded by Gary Douglas in 1990 in Santa Barbara, California [1]. A practitioner lightly touches 32 points on the head, similar in manner to acupressure, a process followers call running the bars [1].

People who use it for self-improvement describe a chain rather than a direct effect on appearance: a quieter mind and relaxed body lead to better sleep, less stress and a calmer expression, which they feel shows in the face and posture. Practitioners also claim clearer thinking, more energy and improved wealth [1].

Wikipedia characterises the movement as pseudoscientific and notes that proponents cite studies which critics regard as poor; scalp-touch relaxation, it says, can also be reached by resting [1]. Complaints and licensing actions involving practitioners are described below.

chain: Less tension in face and posture, per proponents
angle.text: Followers use the bars for relaxation and a calmer sense of self, which they associate with looking more at ease. The wiki records this as a claimed, indirect route; no study has measured appearance outcomes.

paras: In a typical session the practitioner rests fingertips lightly on points of the head, which the system links to themes such as creativity, memory and money. Wikipedia notes that the points are loosely tied to Chinese meridian ideas but assigned to different concepts [1]. Douglas said he learned the Bars from channelled spirits, including Grigori Rasputin [1].

Douglas founded the movement as Access Energy Transformation in 1990, after a bankruptcy in 1993 following a real estate venture [1]. Dain Heer joined in 2001 and Simone Milasas in 2003 [1]. It reached France in 2010 and was reported in 170 countries by 2020, with about 3,000 licensed facilitators in 2024 [1].

Practitioners claim clearer thinking, more energy, better health and more wealth from the Bars [1]. Appearance claims in the wellness community are mostly about stress release and feeling lighter, rather than any structural change.

No studies found on appearance outcomes. Proponents cite small studies on wellbeing; Jonathan Jarry and David Gorski, quoted on Wikipedia, regard these as poor and say no good evidence links the practice to biology, medicine or psychology [1].

In 2024 former members filed a complaint with Australia's ACCC alleging false claims and a pyramid or multi-level marketing structure [1]. In 2018 a Nova Scotia social worker practising Access Consciousness had her licence revoked for inappropriate touching and contact outside the office [1]. Facilitator training was listed at AUD 30,000 with renewal at AUD 17,000 in 2024 [1].

timeline.event: Gary Douglas founds Access Energy Transformation in Santa Barbara [1].
Nova Scotia social worker's licence revoked [1].
Former members file complaint with the ACCC [1].
